newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank sees good inflation outlook next two yrs.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank sees good inflation outlook next two yrs.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday said the outlook for inflation in the coming two years was good.

In its final inflation report for 1996 that coincided with another cut 25 basis points cut in its key repo rate to 4.10 percent, the Riksbank said the outlook for inflation was somewhat more optimistic than in its last report in September.
"The Riksbank now judges that the rate of inflation in 1997 will be just under 1.5 percent followed by about two percent in 1998," the Riksbank said in a statement.
"For 1996 the rate of inflation will be some tenths of a percentage point below the inflation target's lower tolerance interval."
The Riksbank had set an inflation target of two percent with a one percentage point movement in either direction.
The central bank said the lower inflation stemmed from the transitory effects of decreased interest costs and lower import prices.
"These tendencies reflect an enhancement of economic policy's credibility," it said.
The Riksbank said economic information over the past three months confirmed the picture of an economic recovery in Sweden during 1996.
"The main factors have been strongly rising exports and investment," it said.
"Still it is not conidered likely that in the coming two years economic activity will rise above the level of resource utilisation at which inflation is liable to pick up."
The bank said the expected increase in the rate of inflation was mainly explained by diminishing effects of lower interest rates and a stronger exchange rate.
"The Riksbank's main scenario for the coming two years suggests that the monetary stance is relatively well balanced," the bank said.
"The additional room that may exist for lowering the repo rate is limited."
But the bank warned that if wage increases in 1997 and 1998 are the same as 1996 then inflation could be over target.
